summary: MCP server auto-launches Conductor.exe from AppData when not running
rationale: Users should never need to manually start Conductor or run it from source. The MCP checks port 5000 before every API call and launches the exe if needed.

summary: Deleted old Redis Operator exe and DB to prevent fork bomb from VM monitor worker
rationale: The Cowork VM Monitor worker (worker #4) was spawning cascading subprocesses every 30 minutes, exhausting threads/memory. The old Redis Operator.exe in AppData was a separate instance with its own DB causing conflicts.

summary: Removed auto-start registry entry — Conductor launches on demand via MCP or manual exe click
rationale: The HKCU Run registry entry was launching Conductor on every boot, opening extra browser tabs. With MCP auto-launch, the registry entry is unnecessary.

summary: Conductor auto-launch uses tasklist process check + O_EXCL file lock to prevent race
rationale: First attempt only checked port 5000, which races during the exe's 2-5 second startup window. Multiple MCP tool calls would each see 'not running' and launch duplicate instances. Fix: check tasklist first (catches in-flight launches), then acquire an exclusive file lock (os.O_EXCL) before spawning. Double-check state after lock acquisition.

alternatives.reason_rejected: Windows doesn't have equivalent, and user should not need to configure services

constraints_created: Every api() call in the MCP goes through _ensure_conductor()

summary: Worker/chain subprocesses must resolve a real Python via _resolve_python(), never sys.executable. When frozen by PyInstaller, sys.executable is Conductor.exe, which silently reported success for scripts that never ran.
problem: conductor.spec freezes launch.py as the PyInstaller entry point, so in the shipped exe sys.executable == Conductor.exe. app.py built worker commands as [sys.executable, task_path], producing `Conductor.exe user_script.py`. launch.py:main() ignored sys.argv entirely: if Conductor was already on port 5000 it printed a banner, opened a browser tab and sys.exit(0) -> rc 0 -> _task_runner logged "OK ... completed" and wrote success=1 to run_history for a script that NEVER RAN. If the port was free it booted a second full Conductor (the "fork bomb" recorded in dec-002). No python.exe was bundled, and README claimed "No Python required". This affected the product's only sanctioned deployment mode.
why_chosen: Verified empirically before changing anything: simulating the frozen entry point produced success=True, error_msg='', and the user's script demonstrably never executed. Resolution order (CONDUCTOR_PYTHON override, bundled python, py launcher, PATH, Windows registry) covers realistic installs without bundling a full CPython, which would have inflated the installer substantially. Every candidate is probed by actually executing it and is rejected if its name contains "conductor", so the failure mode cannot recur silently. Raising InterpreterNotFound rather than degrading is deliberate: a loud failure is strictly better than a false success for a scheduler whose entire value is telling you whether your job ran.
what_we_tried: Repo's own .context/decisions.json dec-002 recorded a "fork bomb" and fixed it by deleting an exe - treating the symptom (a second Conductor booting) without ever identifying sys.executable as the cause. constraints.json con-001 then banned running from source, which was the only mode that actually worked.
tradeoffs: Conductor now has a hard runtime dependency on a discoverable system Python for .py workers, so the README's "No Python required" claim had to go. Machines with no Python will now see explicit worker failures where they previously saw (false) successes - correct, but it will look like a regression to anyone who trusted the old green ticks.

alternatives.option: Bundle a full CPython runtime inside the PyInstaller build
alternatives.reason_rejected: Large installer growth and a second Python to keep patched; system Python is present on virtually all target machines and CONDUCTOR_PYTHON covers the rest. Still compatible - _resolve_python checks for a bundled python first.

alternatives.option: Make launch.py parse sys.argv and exec the script when given one
alternatives.reason_rejected: Turns the app into an accidental interpreter, inherits none of the venv/site-packages semantics users expect, and keeps the confusing coupling. launch.py now rejects script args with exit 2 instead.

alternatives.option: Only fix _run_script and leave the guard out
alternatives.reason_rejected: Leaves no defence if any future code path reintroduces sys.executable. _assert_not_self makes the false-success class of bug structurally impossible.

constraints_created: Never use sys.executable to run user scripts; always call _resolve_python()
retrieval_hints: why does Conductor.exe report success for scripts that never ran
